solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Too right I hold with Indian cooking!

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the run of letters from too, right and I wraps around another piece

parts.note: taken as written
with and and both mean together alongside

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic diner agreeing loudly that Indian food is the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too right' reads as Australian-style agreement, but it splits in two; 'hold' wraps the first three words around 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tandoori is a style of Indian cooking done in a clay oven, a tandoor.

clue.text: Decorative stuff can retail with a pound off

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: off means taken away from the other piece

parts.note: to retail goods is to sell them
L stands for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A shop can sell its decorations with a pound knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is the container TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittering strips of metallic material used as Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Sister company welcomes one messenger

parts.note: a sister in religious orders is a nun

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A nun's firm greets a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal envoy, an ambassador or messenger of the Pope.

clue.text: Everything bright, presumably, for City

definitions.meaning: if all is bright then nothing is thick: nought, O, plus dense
the Danish city on Funen, birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen

explanation.walkthrough: Read as O DENSE, with O as nought: no one is dense, so all are bright, and 'presumably' flags the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is the third-largest city in Denmark.

clue.text: Measured pressure in wind instrument

indicators.note: in puts the second piece inside the first

parts.note: a reed is a wind instrument such as an oboe or clarinet
strain is stress or pressure

explanation.surface: Steady breath pressure inside a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured speech or action is calm and controlled, as is restrained behaviour.

clue.text: Almost everyone's entertained by a little opera

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a little and some both mean a modest quantity

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: everyone means all of them

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole audience enjoys a short bit of opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter; the 's of everyone's is 'is', and 'entertained by' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome is the one-act opera by Richard Strauss, based on Oscar Wilde's play.

clue.text: Liqueur drunk neat? I decline to go into that

indicators.note: go into means the pieces are placed inside what was rearranged
drunk means the letters are reeling and out of order

parts.note: the sun declines when it sets

explanation.surface: A drinker refuses to take a liqueur straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges the letters to ANTE, and 'to go into' puts the rest inside; 'neat' suggests undiluted spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Gift from European band

parts.note: off can mean from, as in jumping off a wall
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A present sent from a European music group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a RING.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something presented as a gift, often to a deity or a cause.

clue.text: Stopping duty free endlessly turned to trouble

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods

indicators.note: turned means the letters run the other way
endlessly removes the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Halting duty-free sales has caused trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves RE, which 'turned' makes ER, and 'Stopping' puts it in the tax. 'duty free' looks like one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise someone is to worry or trouble them, as in an issue exercising the mind.

clue.text: Name wayward son seen making moonshine

indicators.note: something wayward goes astray, so these letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: A wayward son is caught making illicit liquor in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges SON SEEN into ONSENSE, after N. 'Moonshine' looks like illegal spirits but means foolish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine, besides illicit whisky, means foolish or fanciful talk, the same as rubbish or claptrap.

clue.text: Rubbish heap overshadows centre of Stafford

indicators.note: to overshadow is to loom over and cover, so one piece envelops the other

parts.note: a heap is a pile

indicators.note: the centre of the word picks out its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip looms over the middle of a Staffordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the middle pair, and 'overshadows' wraps the heap around them. Stafford is an English county town.
explanation.definitionFit: Piffle is a mild colloquial synonym for nonsense or rubbish talk.

clue.text: Spy English teacher fairly regularly

parts.note: Miss is how British pupils address a female teacher

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word fairly

explanation.surface: Someone accuses an English teacher of being a spy now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairly regularly' looks like a phrase meaning quite often; 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'fairly', giving ARY.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is an agent sent on a mission, and in older usage a spy or secret agent.

clue.text: Transfer rickety boxes of iron

indicators.note: boxes means contains, so the letters sit inside these two words

explanation.surface: Moving some unstable boxes made of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like a noun but is the verb: TransFER RICkety holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric is the chemistry adjective for iron, from Latin ferrum.

clue.text: Leave before breakfast and dash

definitions.meaning: rise from bed and depart early, before eating
dash means energy and drive, vigour

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase is rising from bed and going before breakfast; as a noun it means vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an idiom for energy and initiative, just as dash means verve.

clue.text: Rakes in close to fortune working with B-lister

indicators.note: working here means being worked over and rearranged
the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Minor celebrities making their fortune hang around with rakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges IN, E (the close to fortune) and BLISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeking man, a synonym for a libertine.

clue.text: Charlie's enthralled by surgeon wiggling bum

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so one letter is inside the other
wiggling means the letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie is captivated as a surgeon wiggles his bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a noun for the backside but is the verb meaning to cadge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum something is to cadge or beg it off someone, informally.

clue.text: Primarily murmuring speaker?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: one who utters words is a speaker

explanation.surface: Someone who mostly talks under their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of murmuring, M, goes before UTTERER; the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mumbles indistinctly is chiefly a murmuring talker.

clue.text: Cut price of delicate material?

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Asking about a reduced price for fine fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut price' looks like a discount, but 'Cut' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to cut or tear flesh deeply.

clue.text: Bold American follows officer around these days

indicators.note: follows means the next piece comes after the others
around means the first piece is placed on either side of the second

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
these days is our age, the present era

explanation.surface: A bold American trails an officer around in the present day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these days' gives OUR AGE, which the C and O of CO surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and courageous are synonyms for brave, unafraid.

clue.text: Devotee captures queen, leading to mate

indicators.note: captures means takes in, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: a fiend is an enthusiast, as in a fitness fiend
R stands for queen, from Latin regina

explanation.surface: A chess fan takes the queen on the way to checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'mate' is a pal, not checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is an informal word for a pal or companion.

clue.text: The man nearly advanced on a woman

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: money advanced is lent

explanation.surface: A man almost made advances toward a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' looks like moving forward but means LENT, as in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is a woman's name, used here as the definition for any female name.

clue.text: Fly east from France, returning twice

indicators.note: twice means the piece appears two times in a row
returning means the letters go back the other way

parts.note: est is French for east

explanation.surface: An insect flies eastward out of France, coming back twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Not the trendy group, for a start

parts.note: the trendy are in, so not in is out
a group is a set

explanation.surface: Uncool kids, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: IN means fashionable, so its opposite, OUT, is 'not the trendy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An outset is the beginning or start of something.

clue.text: Close by hotel with no locks?

indicators.note: by means placed beside the other piece

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
close weather is stuffy, without fresh air

explanation.surface: A stuffy room next to a hotel with no locks on the doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests door security but means tresses of hair, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Locks of hair are tresses, so lacking any is being bald.

clue.text: New mark in test achieves standard

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the first

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
M stands for mark, as in the German currency

explanation.surface: A new mark in a test reaches the required level.
explanation.walkthrough: M for mark, the former German currency, goes inside ORAL, an oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard and normal both mean usual, typical, conforming to the norm.

clue.text: A depression grabs the woman's admirer

indicators.note: to grab something is to take hold of it, so it ends up within

parts.note: a dent is a small depression in a surface
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone feeling low clings to a woman's admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter, someone who admires a cause or leader.

clue.text: After long year missing, journalist is brought home

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind the preceding one
missing means the named letter is left out

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter comes home after a long missing year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective but is the verb YEARN, with Y missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring home a wage is to earn it, so brought home means gained by work.

clue.text: A rare dog barking? Could be violence on the way

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are crazily mixed up

explanation.surface: A rare breed of dog barking at passers-by on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' seems to describe the dog, but as British slang for crazy it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is aggressive behaviour by drivers toward others on the road.
